claims.text: The local Japanese classic catalog models Gold, Silver, to a New World... / 金、銀、新世界へ... with a February 4, 2000 release date.
The local catalog and TCGdex-derived metadata model 96 card rows for Gold, Silver, to a New World..., with no source-gap rows in the local release file.
Gold, Silver, to a New World... is modeled as a Japanese main expansion in the ポケモンカード★neo series, using TCGdex set id neo1.

Gold, Silver, to a New World... matters because it opens Generation II in card form: new starters, baby Pokemon, Lugia, Steel/Metal grammar, Darkness Energy, and Johto-specific creature texture all arrive as one apparatus.

The local deepening queue highlights Meganium, Bellossom, Jumpluff, Heracross, Typhlosion, and Feraligatr; this tranche also hand-authors Pichu, Donphan, Steelix, Skarmory, Lugia, Darkness Energy, and Metal Energy because they teach the release’s new-world grammar.

The local Japanese classic rows for this release do not provide illustrator authority, so this tranche leaves artist coverage unresolved rather than inventing or importing credits without a cited source.

narrative.human_title: Gold, Silver, to a New World... — when Johto becomes playable memory
narrative.why_it_matters: Gold, Silver, to a New World... is the card-game doorway into Generation II: not just new names, but new ways for Pokemon to be young, metallic, dark, legendary, local, and mechanically different. It is one of the cleanest sets for teaching an agent that a card market is built from world grammar, not only famous characters.
